units.Haggai 1:1: In the second year under King Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came through Haggai the prophet, saying: “Speak now to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, and to Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying:
units.Haggai 1:2: ‘Thus says the Lord Almighty: These people say, “The time has not arrived to rebuild the house of the Lord.”’”
units.Haggai 1:3: The word of the Lord came through Haggai the prophet, saying:
units.Haggai 1:4: “Is it time for you to live in your houses with recessed ceilings, while this house has been laid waste?
units.Haggai 1:5: And now, thus says the Lord Almighty: Set your hearts upon your ways.
units.Haggai 1:6: You sowed much and brought in little; you ate, but were not satisfied; you drank, but not to intoxication; you clothed yourselves, but were not warmed in them. The one gathering wages gathered them into a bundle with holes.
units.Haggai 1:7: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Place your hearts upon your ways.
units.Haggai 1:8: Go up onto the mountain, cut wood and rebuild the house. I will take pleasure in it and be glorified, said the Lord.
units.Haggai 1:9: You looked for much, and it came to little; it was brought into the house, and I blew it away. Therefore, thus says the Lord Almighty: Because My house is desolate, while each of you hurries to his own house,
units.Haggai 1:10: therefore heaven will hold back dew, and the earth will withhold its produce.
units.Haggai 1:11: I will bring a sword upon the land and the mountains, upon grain, wine and oil, and whatever the earth produces, upon people and livestock, and upon all the labors of their hands.”

reread_versions.relationship: named prophet and rebuilding leaders in the restoration narrative
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai's opening identifies Haggai, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Joshua son of Jehozadak; Ezra names Haggai's prophecy and the rebuilding work of Zorobabel son of Salathiel and Iesous son of Iosedek. The parallel named participants are retained with each text's spellings.

reread_versions.relationship: second year of Darius as the setting for resumed temple work
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai dates his message to Darius's second year; Ezra says the Lord's house remained idle until that second year. The shared regnal year locates the appeal in the narrative's transition from halted work.

reread_versions.relationship: rebuilding delayed before the prophetic appeal
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai reports the people's claim that the rebuilding time has not arrived; Ezra records that work on God's house stood idle until Darius's second year. The narrative supplies the prolonged stoppage to which Haggai's appeal speaks, without equating external force with the people's stated excuse.
reread_versions.source_text: ‘Thus says the Lord Almighty: These people say, “The time has not arrived to rebuild the house of the Lord.”’”

target_units.text: Then the work of the house of God in Jerusalem ceased, and it remained idle until the second year of the reign of Darius king of the Persians.

reread_versions.relationship: Haggai explicitly identified as the bearer of divine prophecy
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai introduces the Lord's word through the named prophet; Ezra explicitly identifies Haggai as prophesying to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in God's name. This links the named prophetic ministry, rather than merely two anonymous revelation headings.
reread_versions.source_text: The word of the Lord came through Haggai the prophet, saying:

target_units.text: Haggai the prophet and Zacharias son of Addo prophesied a prophecy over the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel, over them.

reread_versions.relationship: contrast between a settled personal house and God's dwelling
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai challenges inhabitants of houses with recessed ceilings while God's house lies waste; David notices that he lives in a cedar house while God's ark remains in a tent. Both contrast domestic comfort with the condition of the divine dwelling, in different historical settings.
reread_versions.source_text: “Is it time for you to live in your houses with recessed ceilings, while this house has been laid waste?

target_units.text: When the king was settled in his house and the Lord had given him possession on every side, away from all his surrounding enemies,
the king said to Nathan the prophet, “Look now, I dwell in a cedar house, while the ark of God remains inside the tent.”
Nathan said to the king, “Go and do all that is in your heart, for the Lord is with you.”

reread_versions.relationship: examination of one's way oriented toward the Lord
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai commands the people to set their hearts on their ways; Lamentations describes the way being searched and examined and calls for return to the Lord. Both connect reflection on conduct with a response toward God.
reread_versions.source_text: And now, thus says the Lord Almighty: Set your hearts upon your ways.

target_units.text: Our way was searched and examined; let us return to the Lord.

reread_versions.relationship: much sowing but little harvest and frustrated crop enjoyment
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai describes much sowing with little brought in and unsatisfied consumption; Deuteronomy's curse describes much seed with little gathered and denied enjoyment of wine and oil. The connection concerns agricultural futility, without assigning Deuteronomy's named pests to Haggai.
reread_versions.source_text: You sowed much and brought in little; you ate, but were not satisfied; you drank, but not to intoxication; you clothed yourselves, but were not warmed in them. The one gathering wages gathered them into a bundle with holes.

target_units.text: You shall carry much seed into the field, and gather little; for the locust shall devour it.
You shall plant a vineyard and dress it, but shall neither drink wine nor rejoice in it; for the worm shall devour it.
You shall have olive trees throughout all your borders, but shall not anoint yourself with oil; for your olives shall fall away.

reread_versions.relationship: eating without satisfaction as covenant affliction
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai says the people ate without being satisfied; Leviticus warns of scarcity in which people eat and are not filled. Both treat food that fails to satisfy as an affliction.
reread_versions.source_text: You sowed much and brought in little; you ate, but were not satisfied; you drank, but not to intoxication; you clothed yourselves, but were not warmed in them. The one gathering wages gathered them into a bundle with holes.

target_units.text: When I afflict you with a scarcity of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven and give back your bread by weight. You shall eat and in no wise be filled.

reread_versions.relationship: same-chapter repetition of the command to examine one's ways
reread_versions.rationale: The command to place their hearts upon their ways repeats the earlier command to set their hearts upon their ways. The repetition frames the account of disappointing labor before the concrete rebuilding instruction.
reread_versions.source_text: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Place your hearts upon your ways.

target_units.text: And now, thus says the Lord Almighty: Set your hearts upon your ways.

reread_versions.relationship: procurement of timber for the Lord's house
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai directs the people to cut wood and rebuild the house; Ezra describes provision of payment and supplies to bring cedar timber for the rebuilding setting. Both join obtaining wood to the temple work, without identifying the mountain in Haggai with a specific place.
reread_versions.source_text: Go up onto the mountain, cut wood and rebuild the house. I will take pleasure in it and be glorified, said the Lord.

target_units.text: They gave silver to the stonecutters and craftsmen, and food, drink and oil to the Sedanin and Sorin, to bring cedar timber from Lebanon to the sea at Joppa, according to the concession of Cyrus king of the Persians to them.

reread_versions.relationship: same-chapter return to the contrast between private houses and God's desolate house
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai attributes the reduced yield to His desolate house while people hurry to their own houses; the earlier challenge contrasts their finished ceilings with His wasted house. The repeated contrast makes the reason for the shortfall explicit.
reread_versions.source_text: You looked for much, and it came to little; it was brought into the house, and I blew it away. Therefore, thus says the Lord Almighty: Because My house is desolate, while each of you hurries to his own house,

target_units.text: “Is it time for you to live in your houses with recessed ceilings, while this house has been laid waste?

reread_versions.relationship: withheld dew and produce contrasted with restoration
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai says heaven withholds dew and the earth its produce; Zechariah promises heaven's dew and the earth's produce to the restored remnant. The same two provisions are denied and then promised in the prophetic rebuilding setting.
reread_versions.source_text: therefore heaven will hold back dew, and the earth will withhold its produce.

target_units.text: but I will show peace: the vine will give its fruit, the earth its produce, and heaven its dew. I will give My people’s remnant all these as an inheritance.

reread_versions.relationship: withholding of dew announced by divine authority
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai announces heaven holding back dew; Elijah announces that no dew or rain will come apart from his prophetic word before the living Lord. Both make withheld dew an announced divine judgment, without equating the episodes.
reread_versions.source_text: therefore heaven will hold back dew, and the earth will withhold its produce.

target_units.text: Elijah the prophet, the Tishbite from Thesbon in Gilead, said to Ahab, “As the Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there will be neither dew nor rain these years except through the utterance of my word.”

reread_versions.relationship: the Lord bringing a sword as judgment
reread_versions.rationale: The native Haggai passage says the Lord brings a sword upon land, produce, people and labor; Leviticus warns that God brings a sword exacting covenant penalty. The correspondence preserves sword language rather than replacing Haggai's word with drought.
reread_versions.source_text: I will bring a sword upon the land and the mountains, upon grain, wine and oil, and whatever the earth produces, upon people and livestock, and upon all the labors of their hands.”

target_units.text: And I will bring upon you a sword exacting the penalty of the covenant. You shall flee into your cities, and I will send death among you; you shall be handed into enemies’ hands.

reread_versions.relationship: the named leaders respond to prophecy by rebuilding
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai says Zerubbabel, Joshua and the remnant listened to the Lord and Haggai; Ezra places the same leaders' beginning to build immediately after Haggai's and Zacharias's prophecy. The connection is the narrative response to prophetic ministry.
reread_versions.source_text: Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and all the remnant of the people listened to the voice of the Lord their God and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the Lord their God had sent him to them. The people feared before the Lord.

reread_versions.relationship: divine presence as the basis of encouragement
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai delivers the Lord's assurance 'I am with you'; Joshua receives courage because the Lord is with him wherever he goes. The shared assurance supports the work or task given in each setting.

reread_versions.relationship: God stirring people's spirits to build His house
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai says God stirred the leaders' and people's spirits and they worked on His house; Ezra says those whose spirits God stirred arose to go and build the Lord's house. Both attribute willing rebuilding action to God's initiative.
reread_versions.source_text: The Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, the spirit of Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of the remnant of all the people. reread_versions.relationship: rebuilding undertaken by the named restoration leaders
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai records Zerubbabel and Joshua coming with the people to work on the Lord's house; Ezra records Zorobabel and Iesous beginning that house's construction with prophetic help. The common names and work establish the narrative parallel.
reread_versions.source_text: The Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, the spirit of Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of the remnant of all the people. reread_versions.relationship: resumption of work within the specified second year of Darius
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai dates the work described immediately before this unit to the twenty-fourth day of month six in Darius's second year; Ezra ends the period of idle work at that same regnal year. Ezra supplies the year, not Haggai's exact month or day.
reread_versions.source_text: on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year under King Darius.

reread_versions.relationship: identified leaders of the temple rebuilding addressed again
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai's renewed instruction addresses Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Joshua son of Jehozadak with the remnant; Ezra names Zorobabel son of Salathiel and Iesous son of Iosedek as the men beginning the rebuilding. The link identifies the addressed leaders in the construction narrative.

reread_versions.relationship: witnesses of the former house confronted with the new construction
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai asks those who saw the former glory how the present house appears; Ezra describes elders who saw the first house weeping as the new foundation is before them. Both make living memory of the first house important to the response to rebuilding.

reread_versions.relationship: strength and courage grounded in the Lord's presence
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai commands leaders and people to be strong and work because the Lord is with them; Joshua is commanded to be strong and courageous because the Lord is with him. The matching assurance undergirds action in each commission.
reread_versions.source_text: But now be strong, Zerubbabel, says the Lord; be strong, Joshua, son of Jehozadak, the high priest; let all the people of the land be strong, says the Lord, and work, for I am with you, says the Lord Almighty,

reread_versions.relationship: strengthened hands for the temple rebuilding work
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai tells the people and leaders to be strong and work; Zechariah tells hearers of the prophets at the founding and building of the temple to have strong hands. Both encourage the rebuilding community's labor.
reread_versions.source_text: But now be strong, Zerubbabel, says the Lord; be strong, Joshua, son of Jehozadak, the high priest; let all the people of the land be strong, says the Lord, and work, for I am with you, says the Lord Almighty,

reread_versions.relationship: the Lord's Spirit as assurance in Zerubbabel's building setting
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai assures the community that God's Spirit stands in their midst and calls for courage; Zechariah's word to Zerubbabel locates effectiveness in God's Spirit rather than great power or strength. The Spirit's presence or agency supports the work in both.
reread_versions.source_text: and My Spirit stands in your midst. Take courage.

reread_versions.relationship: later citation of the promise to shake heaven and earth once more
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai promises once more to shake heaven and earth, sea and dry land; Hebrews quotes the promise to shake earth and heaven once more and reflects on the removal of shaken things. The explicit repeated wording establishes the citation relationship.
reread_versions.source_text: For thus says the Lord Almighty: Once more I will shake heaven and earth, the sea and the dry land.

target_units.text: His voice shook the earth then, but now He has promised, saying, “Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heaven.”
Now “yet once more” indicates the removal of the things shaken, as things that have been made, so that the things not shaken may remain.

reread_versions.relationship: nations' valuable offerings and the glorification of God's house
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai says the nations' choice things will come and His house will be filled with glory; Isaiah describes nations' wealth, gold and offerings arriving, followed by the glorification of God's house. The relationship follows the native plural choice things rather than substituting a singular personal title.
reread_versions.source_text: And I will shake all the nations, and the choice things of all the nations shall come; and I will fill this house with glory, says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: Then you will see and fear and be astonished in heart, for the wealth of sea, nations, and peoples will turn toward you. There will come to you

All Kedar’s sheep will gather to you, and Nabaioth’s rams will come to you. They will be offered acceptably upon My altar, and My house of prayer will be glorified.

reread_versions.relationship: all temple resources belong to God
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai declares silver and gold His; David acknowledges that everything given for God's house comes from God's own hand and belongs to Him. The surrounding temple donations include gold and silver, making the ownership statement materially specific.
reread_versions.source_text: The silver is Mine and the gold is Mine, says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: Who am I, and who are my people, that we had strength to offer willingly unto Thee in this manner? All things are Thine, and of Thine own have we given unto Thee.

Lord our God, all this abundance that I have prepared for a house to be built for Thy holy name is from Thy hand, and everything is Thine.

reread_versions.relationship: the Lord's glory filling His house
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai promises greater glory for the house; Ezekiel sees the Lord's glory enter the house and fill it. The shared house-and-glory image does not establish that Ezekiel's vision is the exact building phase Haggai compares.
reread_versions.source_text: For the latter glory of this house will be greater than the former, says the Lord Almighty; in this place I will give peace, says the Lord Almighty, and peace of soul as a possession for everyone building to raise this sanctuary.”

A spirit lifted me and brought me into the inner court. Look—the house was full of the glory of the Lord.

reread_versions.relationship: divine gift of peace extending to inner life
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai promises peace in the place and peace of soul for those building the sanctuary; Jesus gives His peace and tells the disciples not to have troubled or afraid hearts. The thematic parallel concerns inward peace as a divine gift, not identification of the builders with the disciples.
reread_versions.source_text: For the latter glory of this house will be greater than the former, says the Lord Almighty; in this place I will give peace, says the Lord Almighty, and peace of soul as a possession for everyone building to raise this sanctuary.”

reread_versions.rationale: The oracle is dated to the twenty-fourth of the ninth month; the later instruction repeats that date as the day from which the people should direct their hearts. The repeated date connects the current message with its stated turning point.

reread_versions.relationship: priests charged to distinguish holiness and teach the law
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai asks the priests for a legal ruling; Leviticus charges the priests to distinguish holy from profane and clean from unclean and teach the Lord's statutes. This explains their role in the following holiness questions.
reread_versions.source_text: “Thus says the Lord Almighty: Ask the priests about the law, saying:

reread_versions.rationale: Haggai's priests deny that food becomes holy when touched by the garment edge carrying holy meat; Leviticus calls the sacrifice most holy and says one touching its flesh is sanctified. The comparison carefully distinguishes direct contact with flesh from the mediated contact asked about in Haggai.
reread_versions.source_text: If someone takes holy meat in the edge of his garment and the edge of his garment touches bread, cooked food, wine, oil or any food, will it become holy?” The priests answered, “No.”

reread_versions.relationship: corpse contact as a source of uncleanness
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai asks about someone defiled through a dead person and the priests affirm resulting defilement on touch; Numbers says touching a dead person makes one unclean and explains the need for purification. This supplies the legal basis of the person's condition.
reread_versions.source_text: Haggai said, “If one defiled through a dead person touches any of these, will it be defiled?” The priests answered, “It will be defiled.”

Whosoever touches the dead body of any human being who has died, and is not purified, has defiled the Tent of the Lord; that soul shall be wiped out from Israel. Because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean; his uncleanness is still in him.

reread_versions.relationship: uncleanness transmitted by an unclean person's touch
reread_versions.rationale: Haggai's priests affirm that what a corpse-defiled person touches is defiled; Numbers explicitly says whatever the unclean person touches becomes unclean. This is the contact rule applied in Haggai's question.
reread_versions.source_text: Haggai said, “If one defiled through a dead person touches any of these, will it be defiled?” The priests answered, “It will be defiled.”

reread_versions.rationale: Haggai first asks the people to set their hearts on the time before stone was placed in the sanctuary; the later instruction asks attention from the stated day and the sanctuary's founding onward. The paired directions structure the before-and-after reflection.

reread_versions.rationale: Haggai says God struck the people's labor with barrenness, wind damage and hail, yet they did not turn to Him; Amos describes burning, jaundice and devoured plantings, also followed by failure to turn. case.source_text: In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day of the month, the Lord spoke through Haggai the prophet, saying:
case.reason: The complete date heading, the twenty-first day of month seven, was read in its native order. No sufficiently particular parallel for this dated message was established; a generic revelation heading is not counted as a supported connection.

case.source_text: In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day of the month, the Lord spoke through Haggai the prophet, saying:
case.reason: Ezra supplies Darius's second year as the end of suspended temple work but does not identify the seventh month's twenty-first day given in this source unit. The broad rebuilding chronology was not retained as a distinct match for this date heading.
